thread:
jordan_acme: Hey team — after last night's edge deploy we're seeing a weird discrepancy. Streaming calls show first byte fast (~30-60ms) but end-to-end p99 for some prompts is around 7-9s. The exact same prompt via non-streaming completes ~1.2s p99. Repro steps below.

maria_support: Sorry to hear that, Jordan. Can you drop two request ids (stream + sync) and the curl you used? Also which region and model? :pray:

deply-bot: deploy 2026-03-16T21:12:04 UTC applied: edge-proxy coalescing v2 (coalesce_window_ms=5)

jordan_acme: streaming request id: rq_2361234567_stream
non-streaming request id: rq_2361234567_sync
model: redwood-small-2026-03
region: us-west-2
curl (stream):
```
curl -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-small-2026-03","input":"long prompt ..."}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate?stream=true
```
curl (sync): same but ?stream=false

jordan_acme: client: node-fetch on Cloud Run, reads chunks and renders as they arrive. payload sizes look comparable. Attached logs show first byte at ~45ms then a long quiet period, final token ~8.1s, no retries.

maria_support: initial suspicion: deploy bot shows we changed edge coalescing last night — that can affect flush cadence. tagging eng.

alex_eng: I pulled traces for rq_2361234567_stream and the sync counterpart. Sequence: request hits edge -> forwarded to runtime quickly -> runtime emits tokens steadily -> edge holds for ~4-6s without flushing to client, then flushes multiple chunks. Runtime logs confirm tokens were produced immediately. So transport/edge flushing appears to be the culprit.

alex_eng: The non-streaming path isn't affected because it accumulates the full response and returns it once complete; hence its total latency looks normal. Streaming shows fast initial byte (we send headers and first small chunk) but subsequent small writes are being coalesced and delayed.

tim_sre: Confirmed: coalesce_window_ms default was reduced to 5ms globally to reduce packet overhead. That helps throughput but can harm perceived real-time streaming when token emission is bursty and intermittent — heuristics sometimes wait for more bytes and end up delaying flushes if model pauses.

maria_support: Customer impact is severe. What's a quick mitigation we can apply server-side while eng refines heuristics?

alex_eng: Short-term options: 
- Immediate: per-route/tenant override to set edge_coalesce_ms=0 for this API key (disables coalescing) — no client changes required.
- Recommend-but-not-preferred: client adds header X-Redwood-Stream-Flush: true or moves to HTTP/2 flush semantics. But we shouldn't ask customers to change production clients urgently.

tim_sre: I'll flip a scoped feature flag for acct_jordan to edge_coalesce_ms=0. ETA ~20m.

jordan_acme: Please do that. We can't ship client changes quickly.

alex_eng: Root cause summary: coalescer heuristics were tuned for network efficiency and now incorrectly hold small token writes when the runtime pauses briefly. Non-stream is unaffected because it waits for the full payload.

alex_eng: Long-term fixes: per-route token-aware coalescing, model-adaptive coalesce_ms (lower for models that emit many small tokens), and a canary that disables coalescing for endpoints tagged as low-latency. Also we'll add visibility into chunk inter-arrival patterns.

maria_support: Action items:
- tim_sre: toggle edge_coalesce_ms=0 for api_key=acct_jordan (owner: tim_sre, ETA: 20m)
- alex_eng: add a canary to revert coalescing for streaming routes and start a small rollout (owner: alex_eng, ETA: 2d)
- infra: create alert for stream p95/p99 gap (finish_time - first_byte > 2s) and dashboard for chunk inter-arrival (owner: infra, ETA: 1d)
- maria_support: confirm with customer once mitigation is applied (owner: maria_support)

tim_sre: Update: edge flag toggled for api_key=acct_jordan -> edge_coalesce_ms=0. Please re-run your tests.

jordan_acme: Testing now... re-run shows first byte ~40ms and final token ~1.1s p99 on our side. Looks fixed for us. :relieved:

maria_support: Great. We'll keep the tenant override until eng ships the heuristic improvements.

alex_eng: Follow-ups: instrument runtime->edge chunk sizes and inter-arrival histograms so we can pick better defaults; add header X-RW-Flush-Immediately: 1 as an escape hatch for advanced customers; document streaming flush expectations in the public docs.

maria_support: We'll loop back to the customer and write a blameless postmortem + docs update. Thanks all.

jordan_acme: Appreciate the quick turnaround :clap:
